correctness.rationale: For every positive v, the derivative of log Gamma/IG density is exactly a quadratic divided by positive 2vx², implying at most three density crossings. Equal raw moments of degree 0,1,2 force at least three sign changes via a degree-at-most-two separating polynomial. The resulting +,-,+,- density order, equal mass and equal mean force exactly two CDF intersections with the asserted signs. Stirling, Taylor, and controlled Gaussian-tail integration give the ±1 standardized small-v cutoff. The packaged checker independently calculates brackets and passed 128 diagnostic assertions across 15 v values; these samples are not used as a proof. All densities use the stated IG shape convention and Gamma scale convention.

originality.rationale: A scoped comparison of actual published content and related mathematical records did not reveal a source proving the universal two-CDF/three-density crossing theorem for moment-matched Gamma versus IG kernels together with the small-variance cutoff. The Cambridge probability text already depicts their equal-moment densities, so merely showing a difference or numerical crossing is not claimed as new; the claimed result is the exact all-v count/sign classification and asymptotic location. Unsearched historical stochastic-order results remain a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Cambridge published figure already compares a single matched-moment pair; only the universal CDF classification and its small-variance limit are assessed as new.
Unexamined stochastic-order, reaction-time, or residence-time literature might imply the same theorem. The full Cambridge book and all historical primary papers were not inspected.
Publisher PDF image screenshot retrieval failed; the extracted caption and nearby prose were read, so comparisons to the precise figure geometry are limited.

value.rationale: Both Gamma-reservoir and inverse-Gaussian advection-dispersion kernels are used in hydrologic residence-time modeling. Exact two signed cumulative reversals at fixed mean and variance provide a model-choice benchmark for a policy based on pollutant fraction arriving by a deadline. The two unique threshold locations and their ±1-standard-deviation concentration limit go beyond selected plots or elementary mean comparisons. It does not imply one model is empirically true or that the modeled effect is large in measured catchments.
